summary: Iteration 15: staff role, audit log, PWA. Backend: 32/33 pytest pass (new file test_iteration15_staff_audit_pwa.py). All staff allowed routes work and every other route returns 403 for staff: dashboard, reports, sales GET/PUT/DELETE, expenses, products POST, inventory GET/PUT, stock-movements, payroll, audit-logs, users, role PATCH. If staff sends unit_price=1, the server ignores it and stores qty×product.price (2×120=240) plus the recipe stock deduction. A missing or unknown product_id returns 422. For count: a negative quantity returns 422, an unknown id returns 404, and a save writes the quantity and a 'Stok sayımı' movement. Audit rows are written for admin Ekledi/Düzenledi/Sildi and staff Ekledi/Saydı with the right user_email and role. The collection, user_email and limit filters work, rows are sorted newest first, and a pure member gets 403. PWA files are correct: manifest, icons, sw.js and index.html. UI on mobile at 390px as staff: StaffApp renders and staff cannot reach the dashboard. +/− and the channel picker work, a 2-item sale saves (stock 20→19.5) and the cart resets, and the stock count saves (19.5→18.5). The SW is registered, the title is 'GÖKBOSS POS' and lang is tr. UI on desktop as admin: all 10 nav tabs load. Kullanıcılar shows audit rows with the 'personel' badge, both filters work and the role select can set staff and back. Found 1 failing backend test (staff negative quantity) and a missing Toaster in StaffApp.

critical.issue: No quantity validation. Staff can POST quantity -5 and it is stored with amount -600 ₺, and recipe stock is ADDED back. Staff can push negative revenue or inflate stock. Fix: require quantity > 0 at least for staff (e.g. Field(gt=0) or a check in the staff branch). Staff-supplied id/created_at are also accepted, so a staff user can backdate sales; override them for staff.

minor.issue: The response (response_model=SalesEntry) includes unit_cost (e.g. 2.5 from the recipe). This shows cost data to staff, even though /staff-view hides cost.
Role changes are not written to audit_logs. These are security-relevant actions and should probably be logged.
Staff can sell an inactive product (active=false) through the API. The UI hides inactive products but the backend does not check.

ui_bugs.issue: No <Toaster/> is mounted. Sonner's Toaster only exists in the admin App.js, so staff never see 'N satış kaydedildi', 'sayımı kaydedildi' or any error toast ('Menü ürünü seçin', 'Satış kaydedilemedi', 'Veriler yüklenemedi'). Verified: no [data-sonner-toast] appeared after a save. Fix: render <Toaster position="top-center" richColors /> inside StaffApp.

integration_issues.issue: Items are posted one by one. If item 2 of 3 fails, item 1 is already saved but the cart is not cleared, so a retry creates duplicate sales. With no toast, the staff user gets no feedback at all.

It loads only on mount or when a filter changes, with no refresh after a role change. The user-filter options are built from the already-filtered logs, so after picking a user (or a collection) the dropdown shrinks to just that subset.

action_items: Add a <Toaster/> to StaffApp.jsx so staff get success and error feedback
Validate quantity > 0 for staff sales, and ignore client id/created_at for staff (and ideally check product.active)
Remove unit_cost/stock_moves from the staff POST /sales response (return a reduced model for staff)
Optional: audit role changes; make the AuditLog user-filter options independent of the current filter

Update stale test_iteration14_auth_roles.py: it expects roles == ['admin','member'] and the member account to have role 'member'. Its role-toggle test resets gokboss-member to 'member', which breaks staff tests if both files run together. I restored the account to 'staff' afterwards.
critical_code_review_comments: staff_allowed uses a regex fullmatch on request.url.path; [\w-]+ is fine for uuids
The staff override in make_crud is good. The quantity is still trusted, so negative or 0 values give negative or zero revenue and reverse stock.

index.html changes were not served until the frontend restarted (the CRA dev server cached the old template with lang=en and title 'Emergent | Fullstack App'). I restarted the frontend and it is now correct. The production build is unaffected.
sw.js has an empty fetch handler. Chrome may log a 'no-op fetch handler' warning, which is harmless; installability is OK.
